summary: Practise OHS risk calculations, FMEA, and control prioritization with Excel. Explore the five-day course and its applied curriculum.
lede: Quantitative occupational health risk assessment uses hazard, exposure, and consequence data to estimate workplace risk and inform control decisions. Occupational health and safety practitioners, risk analysts, and operational leads can build risk datasets, compare estimates in Excel, and document assumptions and uncertainty. They can also use FMEA, fault-tree, event-tree, and bow-tie methods to assess scenarios and report priorities and residual risk in a register or dashboard.
audienceIntro: Quantitative OHS risk assessment is relevant when your work requires a defensible comparison of hazards, exposures, consequences, or control options. This course suits practitioners who can bring workplace examples and want to strengthen how they estimate, document, and report risk.
modules: Fault Tree and Event Tree Analysis
OHS Risk Dashboard and Action Plan
prerequisites: Suitable for professionals with working knowledge of workplace hazards, incident reporting, or OHS risk registers. No programming is required; working familiarity with Excel is useful for the calculation exercises. Advanced modeling and AI-assisted incident classification are introduced conceptually rather than taught as implementation skills.
